The Perseid meteor shower has begun, offering skywatchers around the world the opportunity to see up to 100 shooting stars per hour. This annual astronomical event is one of the most popular and spectacular, attracting millions of people to venture outdoors and gaze up at the night sky. The shower is active from mid-July to late August, but the peak viewing period is expected to occur over the next few nights. According to astronomers, the best time to view the meteor shower is between midnight and dawn, when the sky is at its darkest.

The Perseid meteor shower has a long history, dating back to ancient times when it was first observed by Chinese astronomers. The shower is caused by the Earth passing through the trail of debris left behind by the Swift-Tuttle comet, which was discovered in 1862. As the Earth encounters these small particles of ice and rock, they enter the atmosphere and burn up, producing the bright streaks of light that are commonly known as shooting stars. The Perseid meteor shower is one of the most reliable and consistent, making it a favorite among astronomers and sky enthusiasts.

The peak viewing period for the Perseid meteor shower is expected to occur on the nights of August 12 and 13, when the Moon is in its new phase and the sky is at its darkest. During this time, skywatchers can expect to see up to 100 meteors per hour, although the actual number may vary depending on the location and weather conditions. Astronomers recommend finding a dark location with minimal light pollution and allowing at least 20 minutes for the eyes to adjust to the darkness. The meteor shower will be visible from anywhere in the world, although the viewing conditions may vary depending on the location.

The Perseid meteor shower has generated significant interest and excitement among the public, with many people planning to stay up late to catch a glimpse of the shooting stars. The meteor shower is also a reminder of the awe-inspiring beauty and complexity of the universe, and the many mysteries that still remain to be uncovered. As the world gazes up at the night sky, it is a moment to appreciate the beauty and wonder of the cosmos.

As the Perseid meteor shower reaches its peak, skywatchers around the world will be eagerly awaiting the opportunity to see the spectacular display of shooting stars. items.headline: Bias-prone algorithms surpass human recruiters in discriminatory hiring practices, study reveals.
items.teaser: Researchers have found that artificial intelligence is more likely to form biases when hiring than human recruiters, raising concerns abo…
items.story:
Researchers have found that artificial intelligence is more likely to form biases when hiring than human recruiters, raising concerns about the fairness of AI-powered hiring processes. This discovery has significant implications for the increasing number of companies relying on AI to screen job applicants. The study suggests that large language models, which are commonly used in hiring software, can develop their own biases from the data they are trained on. As a result, job seekers may face unfair discrimination, even if the AI system is designed to be neutral.

The use of AI in hiring has become more prevalent in recent years, with many companies adopting automated systems to streamline their recruitment processes. However, this trend has also sparked concerns about the potential for bias and discrimination. Large language models, which are trained on vast amounts of data, can pick up on existing biases and prejudices present in the data, perpetuating them in the hiring process. This issue is particularly problematic, as it can lead to qualified candidates being unfairly rejected or overlooked.

According to the study, large language models can develop biases that are not explicitly present in their training data, but rather emerge from the patterns and relationships in the data. For example, if a model is trained on data that reflects historical biases against certain groups, it may learn to replicate those biases, even if they are not explicitly stated. Experts warn that this can result in a "bias amplification" effect, where the AI system reinforces and amplifies existing prejudices. The researchers found that this phenomenon occurs more frequently in AI systems than in human recruiters, highlighting the need for greater scrutiny and regulation of AI-powered hiring processes.

The findings of the study have sparked concerns among job seekers, civil rights groups, and lawmakers, who are calling for greater transparency and accountability in AI-powered hiring processes. Many are advocating for stricter regulations and guidelines to ensure that AI systems are designed and implemented in a way that prevents bias and discrimination. Companies that rely on AI-powered hiring software are also taking notice, with some reviewing their systems and processes to ensure they are fair and unbiased. As the use of AI in hiring continues to grow, it is likely that this issue will remain a major point of contention and debate.

The issue of bias in AI-powered hiring processes is not limited to any one region or industry, but rather is a global concern that affects job seekers from all backgrounds. As companies increasingly rely on AI to screen and select candidates, it is essential that they prioritize fairness and transparency in their hiring processes. This may involve implementing measures such as auditing AI systems for bias, providing clear explanations for hiring decisions, and ensuring that human recruiters are involved in the process to provide oversight and accountability. By taking these steps, companies can help to mitigate the risks associated with AI-powered hiring and ensure that all job seekers have an equal opportunity to succeed.

As the debate over bias in AI-powered hiring processes continues, it is likely that we will see increased scrutiny and regulation of these systems in the coming months and years. Lawmakers and regulators will be watching closely to ensure that companies are taking steps to prevent bias and discrimination, and job seekers will be advocating for greater transparency and accountability. Ultimately, the goal is to create hiring processes that are fair, unbiased, and effective, and that provide all candidates with an equal opportunity to succeed, regardless of their background or circumstances.

The latest fatality brings the death toll to two, as health officials continue to investigate the source of the outbreak. The first death was reported earlier, and since then, the number of cases has been rising, prompting concerns among residents and visitors. New York City's health department has been working to identify the source of the outbreak and contain its spread.

Legionnaires’ disease is a type of pneumonia caused by the Legionella bacteria, which can be found in water systems, including cooling towers, plumbing, and air conditioning systems. The disease is typically spread through inhaling mist or vapor contaminated with the bacteria, and it can be severe, especially for people with weakened immune systems. The outbreak in New York City is not the first instance of Legionnaires’ disease in the city, as there have been previous cases and outbreaks reported in recent years. However, the current outbreak has raised concerns due to the number of cases reported in a relatively short period.

According to health officials, the number of new cases has been declining sharply in recent days, which suggests that the measures being taken to contain the outbreak may be effective. The city's health department has been inspecting and testing water systems in the affected areas, and several cooling towers have been found to be contaminated with the Legionella bacteria. The health department has also been working with building owners and managers to ensure that their water systems are properly maintained and disinfected. So far, 67 cases have been reported, and the majority of the patients are being treated in hospitals.

The outbreak has prompted reactions from residents, visitors, and business owners in the affected areas, with some expressing concerns about the safety of the water systems and the effectiveness of the measures being taken to contain the outbreak. The city's health department has been providing updates and guidance to the public, and many buildings in the affected areas have been taking steps to inspect and disinfect their water systems. The outbreak has also had an impact on local businesses, with some reporting a decline in customers due to concerns about the safety of the area.

The outbreak of Legionnaires’ disease in New York City has also raised wider concerns about the risks of waterborne diseases and the importance of maintaining proper water systems. The city's health department has been working to improve its surveillance and detection of Legionnaires’ disease, and the current outbreak has highlighted the need for continued vigilance and cooperation between health officials, building owners, and the public. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has also been providing guidance and support to the city's health department, and the outbreak has been reported to the CDC as part of its national surveillance system.

As the investigation into the outbreak continues, health officials will be monitoring the situation closely to ensure that the number of new cases continues to decline and that the source of the outbreak is identified and contained. The city's health department will also be working to provide updates and guidance to the public, and residents and visitors will be advised to take precautions to minimize their risk of exposure to the Legionella bacteria. The outbreak has highlighted the importance of maintaining proper water systems and the need for continued vigilance and cooperation to prevent and respond to public health emergencies.

items.headline: Regulatory framework for autonomous ride-sharing services sparks intense debate among stakeholders nationwide.
items.teaser: Regulatory bodies in the United States are currently engaged in a heated debate over the rules governing the deployment of robotaxis, wit…
items.story:
Regulatory bodies in the United States are currently engaged in a heated debate over the rules governing the deployment of robotaxis, with several major companies pushing for more relaxed guidelines to facilitate the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicles. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has been at the forefront of this discussion, weighing the benefits of increased mobility against concerns over public safety. As the technology continues to advance, lawmakers are under pressure to create a framework that balances innovation with regulation. The outcome of this debate is expected to have far-reaching implications for the future of transportation in the country.

The development of robotaxis has been gaining momentum in recent years, with companies such as Waymo and Cruise investing heavily in the technology. These autonomous vehicles have the potential to revolutionize the way people move around cities, reducing congestion and improving air quality. However, the lack of clear regulations has created uncertainty for manufacturers and operators, hindering the large-scale deployment of robotaxis. The current regulatory framework was largely designed with human-driven vehicles in mind, and lawmakers are now faced with the task of adapting these rules to accommodate autonomous technology. This process has been slowed by concerns over safety and liability, as well as the need to ensure public acceptance of the new technology.

According to industry experts, the key to successful deployment of robotaxis lies in creating a regulatory environment that is both flexible and rigorous. This would involve setting clear standards for safety and performance, while also allowing manufacturers the freedom to innovate and improve their technology. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has proposed a number of guidelines, including requirements for autonomous vehicles to be equipped with multiple sensors and a robust software system. Additionally, the agency has suggested that manufacturers should be required to submit detailed safety assessments and undergo regular audits to ensure compliance with regulations. These proposals have been met with a mixed response from industry stakeholders, with some arguing that they do not go far enough to address safety concerns.

The debate over robotaxi regulations has sparked a lively reaction from stakeholders, with some companies arguing that the proposed rules are too restrictive and would stifle innovation. Others have expressed concerns that the guidelines do not do enough to protect public safety, and that more stringent regulations are needed to prevent accidents. The general public has also been weighing in on the issue, with some expressing enthusiasm for the potential benefits of autonomous vehicles, while others have voiced concerns over the risks. As the regulatory framework continues to take shape, it is likely that these debates will continue, with lawmakers facing the challenge of balancing competing interests and priorities.

The battle over robotaxi regulations is not unique to the United States, with countries around the world grappling with similar challenges. In Europe, the European Union has established a set of guidelines for the development and deployment of autonomous vehicles, while in Asia, countries such as Japan and China are investing heavily in the technology. The global implications of these developments are significant, with the potential for autonomous vehicles to transform the way people live and work. As regulators and manufacturers continue to navigate the complex landscape of robotaxi regulations, it is clear that international cooperation and knowledge-sharing will be essential in creating a cohesive and effective framework for the industry.

As the regulatory debate continues, industry stakeholders and lawmakers are eagerly awaiting the outcome of several key decisions that will shape the future of robotaxis. In the coming months, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is expected to finalize its guidelines, while Congress is set to consider legislation that would provide a federal framework for the regulation of autonomous vehicles. Meanwhile, companies such as Waymo and Cruise are pushing ahead with the development and deployment of their technology, with several major cities already hosting pilot programs for robotaxis. As the industry continues to evolve, it is likely that the battle over robotaxi regulations will remain a major focus of attention, with significant implications for the future of transportation and mobility.

items.headline: Iran's Military Presence on Kharg Island Remains Unwavering Amid US Naval Buildup Threats
items.teaser: Iranian military officials are warning the United States against launching a ground invasion on Kharg Island, a strategic location in the…
items.story:
Iranian military officials are warning the United States against launching a ground invasion on Kharg Island, a strategic location in the Persian Gulf, saying they are prepared to defend their territory. The island, which is home to a major oil terminal, has been a focal point of tensions between Iran and the US in recent years. Iranian forces have been conducting regular military drills and exercises in the region, showcasing their capabilities and readiness to respond to any potential threats. The warnings come amid heightened tensions between the two nations, with the US having imposed stringent sanctions on Iran in recent years.

The history of tensions between Iran and the US dates back to the 1979 Islamic Revolution, which led to a significant deterioration in relations between the two countries. In recent years, the tensions have escalated, particularly with regards to Iran's nuclear program and its military activities in the region. The US has been critical of Iran's actions, accusing it of supporting terrorism and destabilizing the region, while Iran has accused the US of interfering in its internal affairs and imposing unfair sanctions. The situation has been further complicated by the presence of US military forces in the region, which Iran sees as a threat to its national security.

According to Iranian military officials, the country's forces are well-equipped and prepared to defend Kharg Island against any potential invasion. The officials have stated that they have been monitoring US military movements in the region and are ready to respond to any aggression. The Iranian military has also been conducting regular drills and exercises, including missile tests and naval maneuvers, to showcase its capabilities and deter potential threats. The US, on the other hand, has not commented on the Iranian warnings, but has reiterated its commitment to maintaining a strong military presence in the region to protect its interests and those of its allies.

The Iranian warnings have been met with concern from regional and international stakeholders, who fear that any military conflict between Iran and the US could have far-reaching consequences for the region and the global economy. The tensions have already led to a significant increase in oil prices, with many analysts warning that a military conflict could lead to a major disruption in global oil supplies. The international community has been calling for calm and restraint, urging both sides to engage in diplomatic efforts to resolve their differences peacefully. The European Union, in particular, has been working to facilitate dialogue between Iran and the US, with the aim of reducing tensions and finding a negotiated solution.

The situation on Kharg Island is part of a broader pattern of tensions in the region, which has seen a significant increase in military activity and rhetoric in recent years. The US has been working to build a coalition of regional allies to counter Iranian influence, while Iran has been seeking to strengthen its relationships with other nations, including China and Russia. The situation has been further complicated by the presence of other regional players, including Israel and Saudi Arabia, which have their own interests and agendas in the region. As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen how the various stakeholders will respond and what the ultimate outcome will be.

As the standoff between Iran and the US continues, the international community will be watching closely to see how events unfold. The US and Iran are scheduled to engage in diplomatic talks in the coming weeks, which may provide an opportunity for the two sides to reduce tensions and find a way forward. However, with both sides dug in and refusing to back down, it remains to be seen whether a negotiated solution can be found. In the meantime, the region remains on high alert, with many fearing that a miscalculation or misunderstanding could lead to a major conflict with far-reaching consequences. The world will be watching closely to see how the situation develops and what the ultimate outcome will be.

items.headline: A tiny universe in a bottle reveals clues to the origins of life
items.teaser: Researchers have created cosmic dust from scratch by recreating space-like conditions inside glass tubes. The dust contains complex carbo…
items.story: Researchers have created cosmic dust from scratch by recreating space-like conditions inside glass tubes. The dust contains complex carbon-rich molecules built from elements essential to life and produces infrared signals similar to real material found in space. By studying these laboratory samples, scientists can explore how organic chemistry unfolds around stars and how comets, asteroids and meteorites may have carried those ingredients to Earth.

items.headline: The mysterious hum heard around the world may finally have an explanation
items.teaser: The mysterious sound known as The Hum has been reported worldwide for decades, yet its source often remains impossible to find. Researche…
items.story: The mysterious sound known as The Hum has been reported worldwide for decades, yet its source often remains impossible to find. Researchers tested whether people who hear it have exceptional low-frequency hearing or measurable sounds produced inside their ears, but neither explanation fit most participants. The strongest possibility is that many cases involve low-frequency tinnitus, even though the sound seems completely external.

items.story: Fossils from Queensland suggest a newly recognized marsupial order may have survived in Australia for around 35 million years, rewriting part of the story of how the continent's unique mammals evolved. The discovery challenges the idea that Australia's marsupials all came from a single straightforward ancestral lineage.

items.story: The asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs was likely an exceptionally rare CO chondrite from a distant region of the solar system. Its unusual chemistry suggests that planet-cooling dust and debris, rather than sulfur inside the asteroid, may have delivered the deadliest blow.

items.headline: Common antidepressant may ease long COVID’s crushing fatigue

items.story: A low-cost antidepressant may offer new hope for people struggling with long COVID fatigue. In a randomized clinical trial involving 399 adults, fluvoxamine significantly reduced fatigue and improved quality of life compared with a placebo, making it one of the first medications to show meaningful benefits for this disabling condition.

items.headline: Popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
items.teaser: Several popular sugar substitutes may not be as harmless as they seem. Adults who consumed the most artificial sweeteners showed substant…
items.story: Several popular sugar substitutes may not be as harmless as they seem. Adults who consumed the most artificial sweeteners showed substantially faster declines in memory and thinking, especially if they were under 60 or had diabetes. The highest intake was linked to cognitive aging roughly 1.6 years faster than the lowest intake. Researchers stressed that more studies are needed before concluding that sweeteners are the cause.

items.headline: A shattered asteroid may have bombarded Earth 800 million years ago
items.teaser: A catastrophic asteroid breakup may have triggered a huge wave of impacts across the inner solar system about 800 million years ago. The …
items.story: A catastrophic asteroid breakup may have triggered a huge wave of impacts across the inner solar system about 800 million years ago. The debris was launched from near a gravitational gateway controlled by Jupiter, sending fragments toward Earth, the Moon, and Mars. The bombardment may explain ancient lunar craters and could have contributed to major climate and biological changes on Earth.

items.headline: Earth’s biggest volcanic event transformed an entire oceanic plate

items.story: Seismic waves have revealed that the oceanic plate beneath the Ontong Java Plateau was dramatically transformed by the colossal volcanic activity that created it more than 100 million years ago. Researchers found a complex structure of horizontal layers cut through by vast swarms of vertical magma channels, along with unusually slow seismic waves suggesting that deep-rising magma chemically altered the plate itself.

items.headline: NASA’s James Webb catches a supermassive black hole feeding

items.story: JWST has captured unusually detailed images of gas feeding the supermassive black hole at the center of NGC 4696. A vast filament appears to funnel material into an 800-light-year-wide spinning disk, where gas races around at up to 600 kilometers per second. The findings suggest black holes may recycle their own fuel by heating gas with jets and later drawing the cooled material back in.
